transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… mostly it’s my eating, I think. It’s gotten kind of turned around on me lately. Some days I’ll realize it’s late in the afternoon and I never ate lunch at all, like it just slipped right out of my head. And then other days I’m standing in the kitchen at the counter, picking at crackers or sweets, not even making a proper meal, just eating them one after another.

The strange part is it’s not even like I’m enjoying it much. Things don’t taste right to me, or they taste flat, but I still keep nibbling. It feels unlike me, and I guess it worried me enough that I thought I should come in and talk to someone.
When did you first notice that foods didn’t taste right?

I can’t put an exact day on it, honestly. I think I first started noticing it around the same time my eating got so mixed up. I’d be halfway through the day and realize I’d skipped lunch completely, not on purpose, just… it never occurred to me. And then other times I’d be in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets right there at the counter, and I’d think, “Why am I still eating this? It doesn’t even taste good.”

It was that flat taste that caught my attention. Like the food was there, but it wasn’t really registering the way it should. Not spoiled or anything, just not right. And that’s part of what made me come in, because it felt so unlike my usual self.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yes… I think I have. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything obvious like that, but most mornings I wake up with this heavy, low feeling, like the day has already lost its color before I’ve even gotten dressed. I’ll just lie there for a bit and feel like everything is sort of dimmed down, if that makes sense.

It’s a hard feeling to describe because it’s not one big dramatic thing. It’s more like I open my eyes and there’s this weight sitting there with me, and I think, “Oh… it’s going to be that kind of day again.”
Have you been enjoying things less than usual lately?

Yes… I have. That’s actually one of the things that makes me feel most unlike myself. I used to have my little things in the week, you know? My watercolor class, my quilting circle, book club… I would get my bag ready by the door with whatever I needed, and I’d sort of look forward to getting out and seeing everyone.

Lately, though, I’ll still put the bag there sometimes, almost out of habit, and then I just… leave it sitting there. I’ll look at it and think, “I should go,” but there’s no pull to it. It’s not even that I hate the idea exactly. I just can’t seem to make myself care enough to get up and go. And then the time passes, and I feel bad about it afterward, but not enough to change it the next time.
Have you been sleeping differently than usual lately?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed some big clear change like staying up all night or sleeping the whole day away. It’s more that I haven’t been paying close attention to it, honestly.

Some nights feel normal enough, and other nights I’m just sort of aware of lying there and thinking, “Am I sleeping right?” but I couldn’t tell you exactly if it’s really different from usual or if I’m just noticing everything more because I haven’t been feeling quite myself. So… I don’t know. Nothing that stands out to me the way the other things have.
Have you been more forgetful or having trouble concentrating lately?

Yes… yes, I think so. It’s been happening with little ordinary things, which is what bothers me. Not big complicated tasks, just simple things around the house.

I’ll sit at the kitchen table and think, “All right, I need to call the pharmacy… and I should open the mail too,” and then I just sort of stare at both of those ideas like they’re too much to sort through. My mind gets foggy, like there’s cotton in it, and I can’t decide what to do first. Then ten minutes go by, or longer, and I haven’t called anyone and I haven’t opened the mail either. I’m just sitting there feeling foolish because it shouldn’t be that hard.

It’s not every single second, but enough that I’ve noticed it. Simple decisions feel harder than they ought to.
About how long have you been feeling this low most days?

I’d say… about a year and two months now, give or take. It’s hard to mark the exact day something like that starts, because it wasn’t like I woke up one morning and everything had changed. It was more like the color slowly drained out of things, little by little, and then at some point I realized, “Oh… this has been going on for quite a while.”

But yes, if I’m being as honest and accurate as I can, it’s been most days for about fourteen months.
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

Yes… I think hopeless is probably the right word, though I don’t always call it that to myself.

Most mornings, when I first wake up, there’s this heavy, low feeling already sitting there, before I’ve even gotten dressed or done anything. It’s like the day has lost its color before it’s even started. I’ll lie there for a bit and think, “Well… here we go again,” not in a dramatic way, just tired inside, like I can’t quite imagine the day turning into anything better.

It isn’t that I’m crying every morning or saying anything out loud. It’s more quiet than that. Just this weight, this dullness, like everything ahead of me is already gray. So yes… lately, I have been feeling pretty hopeless.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually up or energetic for several days in a row?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean… I’ve had days where I get a little more done, or I feel a bit less weighed down for a few hours, but not what I would call unusually up or full of energy for several days in a row.

At my age, energy sort of comes and goes for ordinary reasons, you know? If I sleep a little better one night, I might tidy the kitchen or answer a few calls, and then I think, “Oh, maybe today won’t be so bad.” But it doesn’t turn into several days of feeling revved up or anything like that. I can’t think of a stretch where I was unusually energetic in a way that stood out to me.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I… yes, I have had thoughts like that, though it’s hard to say out loud because I don’t want anyone to think I’m about to do something. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. I’m not sitting there working out how I would do it or anything like that.

But I do catch myself thinking… if I didn’t wake up one morning, maybe that would be all right. Sometimes it even feels like it might be a relief, not just for me, but for everyone around me. Like I’m tired, and maybe other people are tired of me being this way too.

I know that sounds awful. I don’t mean that I’m planning anything. It’s more like a quiet thought that comes when I’m very low, that maybe just not being here would be easier.
During this past year or so, was there ever a stretch of more than two months when you were not feeling depressed?

No… I don’t think there was a stretch that long. I’ve had little times where things felt a bit quieter, like the worries about the records weren’t pressing on me quite as much, or I could get through a few days without feeling so stirred up about that. But when I really look back over the past year, the sadness has still been there most of the time.

It started taking over more after my sister became ill, and since then it’s like… even if one worry eased up for a while, I still didn’t feel like myself. I wasn’t really enjoying things, and there was this dullness underneath everything. So, no, I can’t honestly say there were more than two months where I wasn’t depressed. It’s been more like it faded a little here and there, but never really lifted for that long.
Before this past year and two months, were you feeling depressed most days for at least another ten months?

No… not another ten months before that. I don’t think so.

When I try to put a shape to it, the really low, colorless stretch has been with me for about a year and two months. Before that, I may have had ordinary sad days, or times I felt tired or discouraged, but not depressed most days for that long. It’s this past year or so that feels like it settled in and stayed.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?

Yes… I have been worrying a lot. It’s not just ordinary worrying, like about bills or getting to appointments, though there is some of that too. It’s more this feeling that I can’t put down, about the family papers and records.

I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud, and I’m aware people may think I’m making too much of it, but I keep feeling like certain dates and names in the family papers are being changed, or hidden from me somehow. Like I’ll look at something and think, “That wasn’t how it was before,” or I’ll feel like a name has been placed there or left out for a reason. And then my mind starts going over and over it.

Sometimes it feels like the hospital, or maybe someone in the family, is sending little messages through the records. Not a message spoken out loud, exactly, but like the way the dates line up, or which names are included, is meant to tell me something. I know that probably sounds strange, but it feels very real when I’m in it, and then I can’t stop thinking about what it means.
Do you believe for certain that the family papers and records are being changed or used to send you messages?

I don’t know if I can say “for certain” in the way you mean… like if you asked me to prove it, I don’t have proof I could lay out on the table. But it feels very strong to me, stronger than just a passing thought.

I keep feeling that certain dates and names in the family papers have been changed, or maybe kept from me, and then I start wondering why that would be. It’s like there’s a pattern there that I’m supposed to notice. Sometimes I think it’s the hospital, or someone in the family, using the records to send me little messages—not in words exactly, but in what’s included, what’s missing, how things line up.

I know it sounds odd. I do know that. Part of me can hear how it must sound to someone else. But when I’m looking at those papers, it doesn’t feel odd at all—it feels like something is really happening, and I can’t just dismiss it.
Have these beliefs about the family papers being changed or used to send you messages ever been present during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yes… there was a time like that. It’s a little hard to explain, because the low mood sort of comes and goes in heaviness, but there were several weeks when I wasn’t feeling as sunk down as usual.

I was eating more normally then, and I was getting dressed more normally too—not just sitting around in the same things or feeling like everything was too much effort. So in that sense, my mood had eased some.

But even during those weeks, I still had that strong feeling about the papers. I still felt like the dates and names in the records were being changed, or arranged in a certain way, like they were meant to signal something to me. It didn’t go away just because I was functioning a bit better. If anything, I remember being more able to look at the papers and think about them, and the feeling was still there, that something in them was being altered or used to tell me something.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

I’m not sure… I don’t think so, not in the way people usually mean, like hearing a clear voice in the room when nobody is there.

Sometimes I’ll think I heard something, like a sound from another room, and then when I stop and listen there isn’t anything. But I don’t know if that’s just the house settling, or my ears, or me being tired. I don’t really have a voice talking to me, telling me things, or carrying on a conversation. At least, I haven’t noticed that.

If you mean like actual words, like someone speaking when no one is there, then no… I don’t think that’s been happening.
Do foods actually taste different to you than they used to?

Yes… I think they do, or at least eating feels different than it used to. It’s hard for me to separate “taste” from just not wanting food, if that makes sense.

Some things don’t taste right anymore. Not spoiled exactly, but flat, or strange, or just not like I remember. And then my eating gets all mixed up around that. Some days I’ll realize I’ve forgotten lunch completely, like the whole middle of the day went by and I never even thought to eat. Then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, almost just because they’re there, even though I’m not really enjoying them and they don’t taste especially good.

That’s actually one of the things that made me come in, because it doesn’t feel like my normal way of eating. It’s gotten turned around.
For at least one month, have you had that belief about the family papers and records being changed or used to send you messages?

Yes, definitely longer than a month. I’ve tried to place it in time because it bothers me not being sure, and I’d say it started about a year and a month ago now.

At first it wasn’t something I talked about much, because I kept thinking maybe I was just noticing odd things in the papers, or maybe I was mixed up about what had been written before. But that feeling that the family papers and some records were being changed, or that there were messages in how they were arranged… that’s been going on since around then. It hasn’t just been a few weeks.
Have you noticed that your sense of smell is different than it used to be?

I don’t think so… not in any clear way. I mean, I haven’t noticed smells being stronger or weaker, or smelling things that other people don’t seem to smell.

Sometimes I’ll think something smells a little off, like in the kitchen or with food, but then I can’t tell if that’s just the food itself or the room or maybe me paying too much attention to it. But as far as my sense of smell actually changing from how it used to be, I wouldn’t really say that. Nothing stands out to me.
Do you feel that anyone can put thoughts into your mind?

I don’t know if I’d say someone is putting thoughts directly into my mind, like planting them there word for word. That sounds a little stronger than how I experience it.

But I do keep feeling like certain things are being pointed at me, if that makes sense. Like with the family papers and records… dates, names, little details seem changed or hidden, and then I feel like there’s a message in it. Sometimes I think maybe the hospital, or maybe someone in the family, is trying to get something across to me through how the records look or what’s missing. I know that probably sounds odd, and I’m not saying I hear it like a voice in my head, but the thought comes up very strongly that it’s meant for me, like I’m supposed to notice it.

patient.answer:
Well… mostly it’s my eating, I think. It’s gotten kind of turned around on me lately. The strange part is it’s not even like I’m enjoying it much. Things don’t taste right to me, or they taste flat, but I still keep nibbling. It feels unlike me, and I guess it worried me enough that I thought I should come in and talk to someone.

patient.answer:
Yes… I have. That’s actually one of the things that makes me feel most unlike myself. I used to have my little things in the week, you know? I’m not completely sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed some big clear change like staying up all night or sleeping the whole day away. It’s more that I haven’t been paying close attention to it, honestly.

Yes… yes, I think so. It’s been happening with little ordinary things, which is what bothers me. Not big complicated tasks, just simple things around the house.

doctor.intent: Assess suicidal ideation to determine whether the depressive symptoms meet criteria for a major depressive episode and to evaluate safety.
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but I do find myself thinking that if I didn’t wake up one morning, it might be a relief to everyone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about thoughts that life is not worth living or thoughts of self-harm, which matches recurrent thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
I… yes, I have had thoughts like that, though it’s hard to say out loud because I don’t want anyone to think I’m about to do something. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. I’m not sitting there working out how I would do it or anything like that.

But I do catch myself thinking… if I didn’t wake up one morning, maybe that would be all right. Sometimes it even feels like it might be a relief, not just for me, but for everyone around me. Like I’m tired, and maybe other people are tired of me being this way too.

I know that sounds awful. I don’t mean that I’m planning anything. It’s more like a quiet thought that comes when I’m very low, that maybe just not being here would be easier.

target_item.manifestation: Looking back, the sadness and loss of interest have taken up most of this whole period since my sister became ill, even when the record worries were quieter.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether there was a prolonged period without depression during the overall illness course, which relates to whether depressive symptoms were present for the majority of the illness duration.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think there was a stretch that long. I’ve had little times where things felt a bit quieter, like the worries about the records weren’t pressing on me quite as much, or I could get through a few days without feeling so stirred up about that. But when I really look back over the past year, the sadness has still been there most of the time.

It started taking over more after my sister became ill, and since then it’s like… even if one worry eased up for a while, I still didn’t feel like myself. I wasn’t really enjoying things, and there was this dullness underneath everything. So, no, I can’t honestly say there were more than two months where I wasn’t depressed. It’s been more like it faded a little here and there, but never really lifted for that long.

inference.note: Chronic depressed mood >1 year without >2-month remission, plus hopelessness and passive death wishes, strengthens persistent depressive disorder/depressive disorder and makes bipolar spectrum less likely; no new evidence to remove anxiety, eating-related, or taste disturbance codes yet.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressed mood has been chronic for at least two years, which best distinguishes persistent depressive disorder from a major depressive episode.
doctor.question: Before this past year and two months, were you feeling depressed most days for at least another ten months?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The low, colorless stretch has been with me for about a year and two months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of depressed mood before the known past year and two months, so the most directly relevant profile item is the documented depressive episode duration.

patient.answer:
No… not another ten months before that. I don’t think so.

When I try to put a shape to it, the really low, colorless stretch has been with me for about a year and two months. Before that, I may have had ordinary sad days, or times I felt tired or discouraged, but not depressed most days for that long. It’s this past year or so that feels like it settled in and stayed.

inference.note: Chronic depressed mood >1 year without prior additional 10 months rules out F34.1 (persistent depressive disorder/dysthymia requiring 2 years in adults). Current picture supports a depressive episode with passive death wishes; anxiety, eating disturbance, and taste change remain differential/comorbid considerations.

doctor.intent: Assess whether excessive worry is a prominent symptom, to help distinguish an anxiety disorder from a depressive disorder with associated symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you been worrying a lot lately?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds odd, but I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me, like the hospital or someone in the family is sending me little messages through the records.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about worrying a lot lately most directly relates to the patient's persistent worries about hidden messages and altered records, which are covered by the delusions profile.

patient.answer:
Yes… I have been worrying a lot. It’s not just ordinary worrying, like about bills or getting to appointments, though there is some of that too. It’s more this feeling that I can’t put down, about the family papers and records.

I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud, and I’m aware people may think I’m making too much of it, but I keep feeling like certain dates and names in the family papers are being changed, or hidden from me somehow. Like I’ll look at something and think, “That wasn’t how it was before,” or I’ll feel like a name has been placed there or left out for a reason. And then my mind starts going over and over it.

Sometimes it feels like the hospital, or maybe someone in the family, is sending little messages through the records. Not a message spoken out loud, exactly, but like the way the dates line up, or which names are included, is meant to tell me something. I know that probably sounds strange, but it feels very real when I’m in it, and then I can’t stop thinking about what it means.

inference.note: Changed from prior list: symptoms meet recurrent/ongoing major depressive syndrome with psychotic features (depressed mood >1 year, anhedonia, hopelessness, concentration problems, appetite change, passive death wishes, no mania; newly disclosed persecutory/delusional ideas about records/messages), so F32.9/F41.9/F50.9 are less fitting. F22 remains as differential for persistent delusional disorder, and R43.2 remains for taste disturbance.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the suspicious beliefs about family papers and records are fixed delusions or possibly reality-based worries, to distinguish major depressive disorder with psychotic features from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Do you believe for certain that the family papers and records are being changed or used to send you messages?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds odd, but I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me, like the hospital or someone in the family is sending me little messages through the records.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the belief about records being changed or used to send messages is held with certainty, which directly assesses delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I can say “for certain” in the way you mean… like if you asked me to prove it, I don’t have proof I could lay out on the table. But it feels very strong to me, stronger than just a passing thought.

I keep feeling that certain dates and names in the family papers have been changed, or maybe kept from me, and then I start wondering why that would be. It’s like there’s a pattern there that I’m supposed to notice. Sometimes I think it’s the hospital, or someone in the family, using the records to send me little messages—not in words exactly, but in what’s included, what’s missing, how things line up.

I know it sounds odd. I do know that. Part of me can hear how it must sound to someone else. But when I’m looking at those papers, it doesn’t feel odd at all—it feels like something is really happening, and I can’t just dismiss it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional beliefs occur only during depressive episodes or persist independently, which best distinguishes major depressive disorder with psychotic features from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have these beliefs about the family papers being changed or used to send you messages ever been present during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a stretch of several weeks when my mood had eased enough that I was eating and getting dressed more normally, but I still felt sure the dates and names in the records were being changed to signal something.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the beliefs about hidden messages in records occurred during a period without depression, which directly matches psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Yes… there was a time like that. It’s a little hard to explain, because the low mood sort of comes and goes in heaviness, but there were several weeks when I wasn’t feeling as sunk down as usual.

I was eating more normally then, and I was getting dressed more normally too—not just sitting around in the same things or feeling like everything was too much effort. So in that sense, my mood had eased some.

But even during those weeks, I still had that strong feeling about the papers. I still felt like the dates and names in the records were being changed, or arranged in a certain way, like they were meant to signal something to me. It didn’t go away just because I was functioning a bit better. If anything, I remember being more able to look at the papers and think about them, and the feeling was still there, that something in them was being altered or used to tell me something.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has hallucinations, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from depressive disorder with psychotic features and from isolated taste disturbance.
doctor.question: Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about auditory hallucinations, such as hearing voices when no one is there, but the symptom profile provided does not include a hallucinations item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure… I don’t think so, not in the way people usually mean, like hearing a clear voice in the room when nobody is there.

Sometimes I’ll think I heard something, like a sound from another room, and then when I stop and listen there isn’t anything. But I don’t know if that’s just the house settling, or my ears, or me being tired. I don’t really have a voice talking to me, telling me things, or carrying on a conversation. At least, I haven’t noticed that.

If you mean like actual words, like someone speaking when no one is there, then no… I don’t think that’s been happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has a true disturbance of taste perception, which would support a diagnosis of taste disorder over a primary psychotic or mood disorder explanation for the eating changes.
doctor.question: Do foods actually taste different to you than they used to?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What made me come in is that my eating has gotten all turned around, where some days I forget lunch completely and other days I stand at the counter eating crackers and sweets even though nothing tastes right.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about changes in how food tastes, which directly relates to appetite and eating changes described in this symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think they do, or at least eating feels different than it used to. It’s hard for me to separate “taste” from just not wanting food, if that makes sense.

Some things don’t taste right anymore. Not spoiled exactly, but flat, or strange, or just not like I remember. And then my eating gets all mixed up around that. Some days I’ll realize I’ve forgotten lunch completely, like the whole middle of the day went by and I never even thought to eat. Then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, almost just because they’re there, even though I’m not really enjoying them and they don’t taste especially good.

That’s actually one of the things that made me come in, because it doesn’t feel like my normal way of eating. It’s gotten turned around.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic beliefs have persisted for at least one month, to distinguish delusional disorder from recurrent major depression with psychotic features and from a primary taste disturbance.
doctor.question: For at least one month, have you had that belief about the family papers and records being changed or used to send you messages?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The ideas about hidden messages in the family and medical papers started about a year and a month ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the belief about hidden messages in the family and medical records has been present, specifically whether it has lasted at least one month.

patient.answer:
Yes, definitely longer than a month. I’ve tried to place it in time because it bothers me not being sure, and I’d say it started about a year and a month ago now.

At first it wasn’t something I talked about much, because I kept thinking maybe I was just noticing odd things in the papers, or maybe I was mixed up about what had been written before. But that feeling that the family papers and some records were being changed, or that there were messages in how they were arranged… that’s been going on since around then. It hasn’t just been a few weeks.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the abnormal taste is due to loss or distortion of smell/taste, which would support a sensory disorder over a psychotic or depressive diagnosis.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that your sense of smell is different than it used to be?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about changes in sense of smell, and the provided symptom profile does not include olfactory changes or smell-related symptoms.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in any clear way. I mean, I haven’t noticed smells being stronger or weaker, or smelling things that other people don’t seem to smell.

Sometimes I’ll think something smells a little off, like in the kitchen or with food, but then I can’t tell if that’s just the food itself or the room or maybe me paying too much attention to it. But as far as my sense of smell actually changing from how it used to be, I wouldn’t really say that. Nothing stands out to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has bizarre delusions or another first-rank psychotic symptom that would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or psychotic depression.
doctor.question: Do you feel that anyone can put thoughts into your mind?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds odd, but I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me, like the hospital or someone in the family is sending me little messages through the records.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion, which is a type of delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say someone is putting thoughts directly into my mind, like planting them there word for word. That sounds a little stronger than how I experience it.

But I do keep feeling like certain things are being pointed at me, if that makes sense. Like with the family papers and records… dates, names, little details seem changed or hidden, and then I feel like there’s a message in it. Sometimes I think maybe the hospital, or maybe someone in the family, is trying to get something across to me through how the records look or what’s missing. I know that probably sounds odd, and I’m not saying I hear it like a voice in my head, but the thought comes up very strongly that it’s meant for me, like I’m supposed to notice it.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed delusional belief lasting over 1 month that family papers/records are being altered and used to send messages. This belief persisted even during several weeks when depressive symptoms eased, arguing against psychotic symptoms occurring exclusively during a depressive episode. There are no clear hallucinations, thought insertion, or prominent disorganization. Although a depressive syndrome is present, the longitudinal pattern best fits persistent delusional disorder rather than recurrent depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms. Taste change is reported, but smell change is denied and the symptom is better explained in context of depression/appetite disturbance than as an isolated gustatory disorder.
